title: §.XIV (5): With Bergen Fathers — Formula Concord above AC; ignore own churches/princes; Formulists keep mutated Art. X
pass_a_gloss: (5.) Those who with the BERGEN FATHERS hold the Formula of Concord — that truly most unhappy apple of strife (ἔριδος) and of all Protestant contention, notorious namely for the doctrines of the Manducation and Omnipresence of Christ's Body in bodily modes — older than the Augsburg Confession itself, which is utterly ignorant of and empty of these Dogmas; nor do they care at all that both formerly and now even by their own — churches and their most pious and learned Doctors, and also Princes and Estates of the Romano-German Empire — it has been contradicted with the greatest zeal, and is still contradicted today by some (see Joh. Crocius in the German Tract from p. 99 and in the Commentary on the Augsburg Confession passim, especially p. 282); and that the Formula of Concord itself has retained the changed Article X of the Augsburg Confession, i.e. not answering to the German Idiom of the Prototype (on account of which changed Article nevertheless the Formulists inveigh so bitterly against the Variata Confession), and has itself undergone most frequent mutations and variations. See the Anhang der ausführlichen Behauptung from p. 26 to 36.
pass_b_english: (5.) Those who with the Bergen Fathers rank the Formula of Concord — that most unhappy apple of strife (ἔριδος) and of all Protestant quarrel, notorious for bodily manducation and omnipresence of Christ's body — older than the Augsburg Confession itself, which knows nothing of those dogmas and is empty of them.

They care nothing that their own side has contradicted it with great zeal both formerly and now — churches and their most pious, learned doctors, and also princes and estates of the Romano-German Empire — and that some still contradict it today (Crocius, German tract from p. 99; Commentary on the Augsburg Confession passim, esp. p. 282).

Nor do they care that the Formula itself kept the changed Article X of the Augsburg Confession — which does not match the German of the prototype — the very change for which Formulists attack the Variata so bitterly — and that the Formula itself has suffered very frequent mutations and variations.
See the Anhang der ausführlichen Behauptung, pp. 26–36.
source_text: (5.) Qui cum PATRIBUS BERGENSIBUS Formulam Concordiae, verum istud ἔριδος omnisque contentionis Protestanticæ pomum infaustissimum, quippe de Manducatione & Omnipraesentia Corporis Christi Corporalibus famosum dogmatibus, ipsâ Augustana Confessione, horum Dogmatum penitus ignara vacuâq;, antiquiorem ducunt; nec quicquam morantur, tàm olim, quàm nunc, etiam à suis, cùm Ecclesiis, harumque Doctoribus piissimis atque doctissimis, tum Principibus & Imperii Romano-Germanici Statibus, maximo cùm zelo contradictum esse, hodieque à nonnullis contradici, (vid. Joh. Crocium in Tractatu Germanico à pag. 99. & in Comment. August. Confess. passim, praecipuè pag. 282.) ipsam etiam Formulam Concordiae, tam mutatum August. Confessionis Articulum X., i. e. Germanico Idiomati Prototypi haud respondentem, (propter quem tamen Articulum mutatum, adeò acerbè in Variatam Confessionem Formulistae invehuntur) retinuisse, quam ipsam per se creberrimas mutationes ac variationes passam esse. Vid. Anhang der ausführlichen Behauptung à pag. 26. ad 36.
